newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco stocks fall on U.S. court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco stocks fall on U.S. court ruling.

text.p: Shares of tobacco stocks fell on Friday morning after a U.S. judge ruled that the Food and Drug Administration has some authority to regulate the industry.
Traders said the ruling was viewed as mixed, but more negative for the tobacco industry.

Shares of Philip Morris Cos Inc fell 1-7/8 to 39-3/4, RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, owner of R.J. Reynolds, dropped 1-7/8 to 29-3/4, and Loews Corp, which owns the Lorillard tobacco unit, declined 1-3/8 to 90-1/4. UST Inc was off 5/8 to 25-5/8.
U.S. District Court Judge William Osteen ruled on Friday that the FDA can regulate the sales and labelling of cigarettes, but cannot make regulations on promotion and advertsing of tobacco products.
"We're hearing it's a mixed ruling, but more on the downside," said Paul Diamond, a trader at Bankers Trust.
